title: Complete complex one-magnon Jordan classification
status: Proved finite-sector classification with exact Gaussian-rational examples; classical framework, no global novelty claim
summary: The simple-critical-point qualification in S010 can be removed. For arbitrary distinct complex spin-1/2 sites, multiplicities of the roots of p′ determine all Jordan block sizes in the one-magnon sector. One explicit local coordinate turns the Bethe vector’s derivatives into a Jordan chain of the correct length. The chains exhaust the sector, and every Hamiltonian generates the same finite commuting algebra after polynomial interpolation.
definitions: Retain p(x)=∏_(j=1)^n(x−z_j), H_i and E_i⁰ from S010, with all physical sites distinct. A critical root w_r has multiplicity m_r as a root of p′. Since p has simple roots, p(w_r)≠0; Σ_r m_r=n−1.
Fix any Hamiltonian index i. At w_r write a=1/(w_r−z_i), use local coordinate q=1/(w−z_i)−a, and define w(q)=z_i+1/(a+q). Expand v(w(q))=Σ_(k≥0)V_(r,k)q^k near q=0.

A length-m Jordan chain for H−E is a list V₀,…,V_(m−1) with (H−E)V₀=0 and (H−E)V_k=V_(k−1) for k≥1. No factorial is missing: V_k is the Taylor coefficient, equivalently the kth derivative divided by k!.

result.name: Critical multiplicity equals Jordan length for every H_i
result.statement: On the n-dimensional one-magnon space, each H_i has one uniform-descendant block of size one and eigenvalue E_i⁰, together with exactly one block of size m_r and eigenvalue E_i(r)=E_i⁰+1/(w_r−z_i) for each distinct critical root w_r. Consequently H_i is diagonalizable exactly when p′ is squarefree, and its minimal polynomial equals its characteristic polynomial of degree n. With A_i=H_i−E_i⁰I, one has A_j=A_i[I+(z_i−z_j)A_i]⁻¹. The characteristic polynomial is χ_Hi(λ)=u^n p′(z_i+1/u)/p′(z_i), u=λ−E_i⁰, interpreted by polynomial expansion. The unital algebra generated by the H_j is C[H_i], isomorphic to C×∏_r C[q]/(q^(m_r)).
result.proof:
The exact off-shell identity is H_i v(w)=(E_i⁰+a_i(w))v(w)−a_i(w)B(w)e_i, with B=p′/p. At a multiplicity-m critical root, B(w) vanishes to order m. The local coordinate q is valid because a_i′(w_r)=−a²≠0, and its inverse is the displayed rational function. Moreover E_i(w(q))=E_i(r)+q exactly. Thus (H_i−E_i(r))v(w(q))=q v(w(q))+O(q^m). Equating Taylor coefficients through q^(m−1) gives the claimed chain. It is independent: if a linear relation has highest nonzero coefficient at V_k, applying (H_i−E_i(r))^k leaves that coefficient times V₀, a contradiction because V₀≠0. Distinct critical roots have distinct E_i(r), since w↦1/(w−z_i) is injective; none equals E_i⁰. Their generalized eigenspaces and the uniform vector are therefore independent. Their dimensions total 1+Σm_r=n, so they form a complete basis and no larger or additional block can exist.

For any other j, put d=z_i−z_j and A=1+da. This A is nonzero because w_r is not a physical site. In the same coordinate, a_j(w(q))=(a+q)/(A+dq)=a_j(w_r)+Σ_(ℓ≥1)c_jℓ q^ℓ, where c_jℓ=(−d)^(ℓ−1)/A^(ℓ+1). The off-shell remainder still has order m. Hence H_j on the chain is E_j(r)I+Σ_(ℓ=1)^(m−1)c_jℓ N^ℓ, with NV_k=V_(k−1). Its linear coefficient is c_j1=A^(−2)≠0, so its nilpotent part is N times an invertible polynomial in N and has the same Jordan length and generalized-eigenspace flags. Equivalently these jets give A_j=A_i(I+dA_i)⁻¹ on each block and on the uniform vector. The denominator is invertible: its critical eigenvalues are (w_r−z_j)/(w_r−z_i), all nonzero, and its uniform eigenvalue is one. An inverse of this finite matrix is polynomial in A_i, giving C[H_i] as the entire generated algebra. Finally χ=u∏_r(u−1/(w_r−z_i))^(m_r); substituting the factorization p′(x)=n∏_r(x−w_r)^(m_r) gives the displayed polynomial formula. The degree-n minimal polynomial and the Chinese remainder theorem yield the algebra decomposition. This proves the entire finite-sector classification, including its nonsemisimple cases.

example.setup: Take four physical sites (1,−1,i,−i), so p=x⁴−1 and p′=4x³. Fix i to be the site z_i=1.
example.calculation:
There is one critical root w=0 of multiplicity three. Its chain coefficients are V₀=(−1,1,i,−i), V₁=(1,1,−1,−1), V₂=(0,2,−1−i,−1+i). The uniform vector and these three vectors have rank four. The eigenvalues are E_j⁰=3/(4z_j) and E_j=−1/(4z_j). In particular H_i has characteristic and minimal polynomial (λ−3/4)(λ+1/4)³. On Q=I−uuᵀ/4, N=(H_i+I/4)Q obeys N³=0 and N²≠0. All equations are checked exactly in Q(i).

A mixed-multiplicity example uses eight distinct sites ±1,±i,±2,±2i, giving p=(x⁴−1)(x⁴−16)=x⁸−17x⁴+16 and p′=4x³(2x⁴−17). The critical multiplicities are three at zero and one at each of four nonzero roots. Thus each H_i has block sizes 3,1,1,1,1,1, including the uniform block. At base site1, E_i⁰=37/60 and E_i(0)=−23/60. If q=λ−37/60, its characteristic polynomial is (λ−37/60)(λ+23/60)³[17q⁴−2(q+1)⁴]/15. The verifier independently calculates the full 8×8 characteristic polynomial by trace/Newton identities over Q(i), checks this factorization and the length-three chain. The four remaining factors have distinct roots because the map w↦1/(w−1) is injective on the four simple roots of 2w⁴−17.
example.conclusion: The multiplicity-three and mixed examples verify higher Jordan lengths and coexistence of simple and nonsimple blocks. The arbitrary-n result is supplied by the proof, not extrapolated from those matrices.

limits: This classification concerns the one-magnon sector for distinct physical sites and the stated spin-1/2 quadratic Gaudin Hamiltonians. It does not settle multi-magnon completeness, higher representations, collisions of physical sites, or a global Langlands correspondence. The direct-product algebra is a finite spectral algebra, not a claim that a general moduli space has been constructed.
extension: In multi-magnon sectors, root-root interactions and admissibility conditions prevent this one-coordinate argument from being transferred unchanged. An appropriate next problem is to seek an equally explicit off-shell jet construction on a fixed small multiplicity space and compare it against an independently computed joint Jordan form.

references.label: Frenkel Gaudin model and opers for the general setting
